helm-values.affinity.description:
Kubernetes Affinity. For more information, see [Affinity v1 core](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.27/#affinity-v1-core).
For example:
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
   requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
     nodeSelectorTerms:
     - matchExpressions:
       - key: foo.bar.com/role
         operator: In
         values:
         - master

helm-values.app.extraArgs.description: Extra command line arguments passed to vault-issuer.

helm-values.app.issuer.ambientCredential.description:
Allow namespaced Issuers to authenticate with credentials drawn from the controller's environment, such as instance metadata or IRSA, rather than from the Issuer's spec.

This is off by default: anyone who can create an Issuer in any namespace could otherwise borrow the controller's cloud identity.

helm-values.app.issuer.clusterAmbientCre.description: Allow ClusterIssuers to authenticate with credentials drawn from the controller's environment. ClusterIssuers are cluster-scoped and therefore managed by cluster administrators, so this is on by default.

helm-values.app.issuer.clusterResourceNa.description:
The namespace Secrets referenced by a ClusterIssuer are read from.

Namespaced Issuers always read their Secrets from their own namespace; this setting only applies to cluster-scoped Issuers, which have no namespace of their own. Defaults to the namespace vault-issuer is installed into.

helm-values.app.issuer.maxRetryDuration.description: How long a CertificateRequest is retried after a transient signing error, measured from when the request was created. Once exceeded, the request fails and cert-manager creates a new one.

helm-values.app.leaderElection.enabled.description: Whether to enable leader election for vault-issuer.

helm-values.app.leaderElection.leaseDura.description:
The duration that non-leader candidates will wait to force acquire leadership. The default should be sufficient in a healthy cluster but can be slightly increased to prevent vault-issuer from restart-looping when the
API server is overloaded.

helm-values.app.leaderElection.renewDead.description:
The interval between attempts by the acting leader to renew a leadership slot before it stops leading. This MUST be less than or equal to the lease duration. The default should be sufficient in a healthy cluster but can be slightly increased to prevent vault-issuer from restart-looping when the
API server is overloaded.

helm-values.app.logFormat.description: The format of vault-issuer logging. Accepted values are text or json.

helm-values.app.logLevel.description: The verbosity of vault-issuer logging. This takes a value from 1-5, with the higher value being more verbose.

helm-values.app.metrics.port.description: The port for exposing Prometheus metrics on 0.0.0.0 on path '/metrics'.

helm-values.app.metrics.service.enabled.description: Create a Service resource to expose the metrics endpoint.

helm-values.app.metrics.service.ipFamili.description: Sets the families that should be supported and the order in which they should be applied to ClusterIP as well. Can be IPv4 and/or IPv6.

helm-values.app.metrics.service.ipFamily.description: Set the ip family policy to configure dual-stack see [Configure dual-stack](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/dual-stack/#services)

helm-values.app.metrics.service.servicem.description: Create a Prometheus ServiceMonitor for vault-issuer.

EndpointAdditionalProperties allows setting additional properties on the endpoint such as relabelings, metricRelabelings etc.

For example:
endpointAdditionalProperties:
 relabelings:
 - action: replace
   sourceLabels:
   - __meta_kubernetes_pod_node_name
   targetLabel: instance
The interval to scrape the metrics.
Additional labels to add to the ServiceMonitor.
Sets the value of the "prometheus" label on the ServiceMonitor. This is used so that separate Prometheus instances can select different ServiceMonitors using labels.
The timeout for a metrics scrape.

helm-values.app.metrics.service.type.description: The Service type to expose metrics.

helm-values.app.podAnnotations.description: Pod annotations to add to vault-issuer pods.

helm-values.app.podLabels.description: Pod labels to add to vault-issuer pods.

helm-values.app.readinessProbe.path.description: The path on which to expose the vault-issuer HTTP readiness probe using the default network interface.

helm-values.app.readinessProbe.port.description: The container port on which to expose the vault-issuer HTTP readiness probe using the default network interface.

helm-values.app.securityContext.description: Security Context to be set on the vault-issuer app container. For more information, see [Configure a Security Context for a Pod or Container](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/).

helm-values.automountServiceAccountToken.description: Automounting API credentials for the vault-issuer pod. Required: the controller talks to the Kubernetes API.

helm-values.commonAnnotations.description: Annotations to apply to all resources

helm-values.commonLabels.description: Labels to apply to all resources

helm-values.enabled.description:
Field to optionally disable installation of the chart when wrapping it as a dependency in another chart.
This matches the helm best practices:
https://helm.sh/docs/chart_best_practices/dependencies/#conditions-and-tags

helm-values.extraObjects.description:
Extra manifests to be deployed. This is useful for deploying additional resources that are not part of the chart.
For example:
extraObjects:
 - apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
   kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
   metadata:
     name: vault-issuer
     namespace: cert-manager
   spec:
     endpointSelector:
       matchLabels:
         io.cilium.k8s.policy.serviceaccount: vault-issuer
     egress:
       - toEntities:
           - kube-apiserver

helm-values.global.rbac.create.description: Create the ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding, Roles and RoleBindings that vault-issuer needs.

helm-values.image.digest.description:
Target image digest. Override any tag, if set.
For example:
digest: sha256:0e072dddd1f7f8fc8909a2ca6f65e76c5f0d2fcfb8be47935ae3457e8bbceb20

helm-values.image.name.description:
The image name for vault-issuer.
This is used (together with `imageRegistry` and `imageNamespace`) to construct the full image reference.

helm-values.image.repository.description:
Full repository override (takes precedence over `imageRegistry`,
`imageNamespace`, and `image.name`).
Example: quay.io/jetstack/vault-issuer

helm-values.image.tag.description: Override the image tag to deploy by setting this variable. If no value is set, the chart's appVersion is used.

helm-values.imageNamespace.description:
The repository namespace used for vault-issuer images by default.
Examples:
- jetstack
- cert-manager

helm-values.imagePullSecrets.description: For Private docker registries, authentication is needed. Registry secrets are applied to the service account.

helm-values.imageRegistry.description: The container registry used for vault-issuer images by default. This can include path prefixes (e.g. "artifactory.example.com/docker").

helm-values.namespace.description:
The namespace to install vault-issuer into.
If not set, the namespace of the release is used.
This is helpful when installing vault-issuer as a chart dependency (sub chart).

helm-values.nodeSelector.description: Configure the nodeSelector; defaults to any Linux node (vault-issuer doesn't support Windows nodes)

helm-values.podDisruptionBudget.enabled.description:
Enable or disable the PodDisruptionBudget resource.

This prevents downtime during voluntary disruptions such as during a Node upgrade. For example, the PodDisruptionBudget will block `kubectl drain` if it is used on the Node where the only remaining vault-issuer
Pod is currently running.

helm-values.podDisruptionBudget.maxUnava.description:
This configures the maximum unavailable pods for disruptions. It can either be set to an integer (e.g. 1) or a percentage value (e.g. 25%).
It cannot be used if `minAvailable` is set.

helm-values.podDisruptionBudget.minAvail.description:
This configures the minimum available pods for disruptions. It can either be set to an integer (e.g. 1) or a percentage value (e.g. 25%).
It cannot be used if `maxUnavailable` is set.

helm-values.podSecurityContext.description: Security Context to be set on the vault-issuer Pod. For more information, see [Configure a Security Context for a Pod or Container](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/).

helm-values.priorityClassName.description:
Configure the priority class of the pod. For more information, see
[PriorityClass](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/pod-priority-preemption/#priorityclass).

helm-values.replicaCount.description:
The number of replicas of vault-issuer to run.

Leader election is enabled, so only one replica reconciles at a time; the others stand by.

For example:
 Use integer to set a fixed number of replicas
replicaCount: 2
Use null, if you want to omit the replicas field and use the Kubernetes default value.
replicaCount: null
Use a string if you want to insert a variable for post-processing of the rendered template.
replicaCount: ${REPLICAS_OVERRIDE:=3}

helm-values.resources.description:
Kubernetes pod resources for vault-issuer.

For example:
resources:
  limits:
    cpu: 100m
    memory: 128Mi
  requests:
    cpu: 100m
    memory: 128Mi

helm-values.revisionHistoryLimit.description:
The number of old ReplicaSets to retain to allow rollback.
If set to 0, no old ReplicaSets are retained.

helm-values.serviceAccount.annotations.description: Annotations to add to the ServiceAccount, for example to bind a cloud identity to it.

helm-values.serviceAccount.automountServ.description: Automount API credentials for a Service Account.

helm-values.serviceAccount.create.description: Specifies whether a service account should be created.

helm-values.serviceAccount.name.description:
The name of the service account to use.
If not set and create is true, a name is generated using the name template.

helm-values.tolerations.description:
List of Kubernetes Tolerations, if required. For more information, see
[Toleration v1 core](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.27/#toleration-v1-core).
For example:
tolerations:
- key: foo.bar.com/role
  operator: Equal
  value: master
  effect: NoSchedule

helm-values.topologySpreadConstraints.description:
List of Kubernetes TopologySpreadConstraints. For more information, see
[TopologySpreadConstraint v1 core](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.27/#topologyspreadconstraint-v1-core).
For example:
topologySpreadConstraints:
- maxSkew: 2
  topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
  whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
  labelSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: vault-issuer

helm-values.volumeMounts.description: Additional volume mounts to add to the vault-issuer container.

helm-values.volumes.description: Additional volumes to add to the vault-issuer pod.
